reviewed_version: arXiv:2211.07213v1, 14 November 2022, 50 pages; journal final not acquired or compared
summary: The weak topology of random finite measures controls expected linear tests, not expected same-outcome self-products. The asserted truncated-energy convergence in Proposition 5.1 is false as an implication of the stated convergence and bounds. No counterexample to the dimension formula is claimed.

problems.claim: In the proof of Proposition 5.1, bounded continuity of kappa wedge delta_hat^(-h) and weak convergence of random finite measures are used to infer convergence of expected double integrals against their same-outcome self-products.

location.exact_locator: p.31, first display after the uniform expected-energy estimate; p.29 eq.(20) states the linear convergence

assumptions: X compact Floyd compactification of the free group F_2 with lambda=3/4 and isolated vertices
eta_n uniform on 2^n positive words of depth n; eta Bernoulli boundary measure
Z_n independent Bernoulli(1/2); chi_n=2 Z_n eta_n; chi=eta
Random masses bounded by 2; mean mass 1; Omega-marginals at most 2P; supports escape every finite vertex set
Same diagonal modification as p.30: delta_hat(x,x)=lambda^|x| at vertices, zero at boundary; h=1
problems.check: For every bounded random continuous f, A_n=int f d eta_n -> A=int f d eta in L1. Cylinder approximation gives E[(2Z_n-1)A]->0, proving exactly Definition A.12 convergence. With kappa=1/8 the truncated kernel is constant, so expected prelimit energy is 1/4, whereas limiting-measure energy is 1/8.
problems.finite_evidence: Exact Fraction enumeration of all pairs of positive words at depths 1-5 matches the analytic energy formula; full-energy bound checked at depths 1-64; finite-cylinder independence at lengths 1-6; eq.(19)-style truncation normalization at depths 1-7. General convergence is proved analytically, not inferred from finite checks.
problems.counterevidence: The example preserves compactness, nonzero limiting mass, boundary support and uniform full energy. Its limiting measure has finite energy. It does not refute the prelimit energy estimate, the compactness theorem, the dimension formula, or an additional BRW-specific convergence lemma if separately proved. These random subsets are not asserted to be BRW traces.
problems.correction: Prove an applicable one-sided energy bound, construct a different limit with controlled products, or supply sufficient additional structure for the actual branching measures. The replacement must preserve nonzero mass and random support.
problems.repair_verification: No complete repair for the paper's random measures certified. Merely replacing equality by an unproved inequality is insufficient.
dependency: p.33 analogous measure construction for Proposition 5.2
problems.impact: Major for a verified invalid derivation materially tied to the central dimension theorem; no claim that the theorem is false or the entire paper fails.

clarifications.claim: The tree branch-point distance is 2n-2k, not 2n-k within a fixed additive constant.

location.exact_locator: last display p.30 and the distance-window restriction at top of p.31

assumptions: x=a^k b^k and y=a^(2k), both depth n=2k
Approximate branch-point choices change k by at most a bounded amount
clarifications.check: Exact common-prefix identity d(x,y)=2n-2k; discrepancy from printed center is k and cannot be absorbed by a fixed constant.
clarifications.counterevidence: The desired weighted pair-count exponent 2n-k is compatible with correct geometry: k+2(n-k)=2n-k. Thus the same intended geometric energy ratio can survive the local correction.
clarifications.correction: Correct the distance center/window; retain the distinction between distance and Green-weight exponent.
clarifications.impact: Local formula correction, not a separately established substantive failure of the prelimit energy bound for all relatively hyperbolic groups.

decisive_checks.result: Deterministic prefix coupling plus L1 martingale cylinder approximation proves Definition A.12 convergence.
Expected prelimit truncated energy 1/4 versus limit energy 1/8; subnet selection cannot change this.
Explicit geometric series bounds expected energies by 7/2 and yields distinct full-energy limits 3/8 and 3/16.
Critical r=R reached through continuity; finite-variance estimates are followed by offspring truncation, not silently imposed on the main theorem.

limitations: The entire 50-page preprint text was read; this is not full certification of every proof or external result.
Full logarithmic tracking argument and all cited external theorems were not independently reconstructed.
Counterexample refutes the stated topological inference; it is not a BRW realization or a counterexample to the dimension formula.
Journal 53(2):391-452 has 62 pages and was not acquired or compared.
Bounded target/version/correction/supplement search did not identify a separate relevant correction or supplement; official article security check, HAL denial, and issue-PDF timeout were preserved.
Initial review is not independent acceptance.
repair_verification: No complete repair of Proposition 5.1 certified.
